questions.q: Identify the word stress on 'present' when it is used as a Noun (e.g., 'I bought a present').
questions.explain: In English, two-syllable words that can be both nouns and verbs usually have the stress on the first syllable for the noun ('PRE-sent') and the second syllable for the verb ('pre-SENT').
questions.exam: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q: Where is the primary stress located in the word 'respect'?
questions.explain: The word 'respect' (whether a noun or a verb) carries primary stress on the second syllable: re-SPECT.
questions.exam: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q: When the word 'record' is used as a Noun (e.g., 'He broke the world record'), which syllable receives the primary stress?
questions.explain: As a noun, the stress falls on the first syllable (RE-cord). When used as a verb (e.g., 'Please record this'), the stress falls on the second syllable (re-CORD).
questions.exam: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q: Where is the stress placed on the word 'project' when it acts as a Verb (e.g., 'The light will project onto the wall')?
questions.explain: For the verb form, the primary stress lands on the second syllable (pro-JECT). The noun form has the stress on the first syllable (PRO-ject).
questions.exam: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral
questions.subject: English Studies
